text:
Nikita Kucherov scored three times in a 8-3 Tampa Bay rout, and the night carried a few other marks with it. John Carlson picked up four assists and reached 800 career points. Sam O'Reilly, the 32nd pick in the 2024 draft who spent last season with the London Knights, collected his first NHL point on Yanni Gourde's goal in the second period. Kucherov's trio came in the third: a backhand 1:25 in, a slap shot at 4:11, and a power-play slap shot at 14:13.

The score badly misstates how the game was played. Buffalo had 61 shot attempts to Tampa Bay's 34 and 31 shots on goal to 22. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, finished almost level, 3.44 for TBL and 3.37 for BUF. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, was 52 percent for Tampa Bay and 48 for Buffalo. The Lightning built their lead in the first period, when they out-chanced the Sabres 1.95 to 0.76, and were up 4-0 before Josh Doan scored on the power play late in the second. Buffalo owned the rest of the game in chances, and Tage Thompson's slap shot made it 4-3 just 33 seconds into the third on what was a 2 percent look.

Then the margin opened. Kucherov scored 52 seconds after Thompson, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed 2.3 goals more than his shots deserved before giving way to Colten Ellis. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 28 of 31 for Tampa Bay. The facts here don't include standings or streaks, but Buffalo spent a night out-shooting the team that beat it by five.
